sections.heading: Introduction

sections.logic: Operational need -> horizon and data gap -> comparison objective -> prior methods

sections.logic: Data integration -> feature construction -> chronological development -> model tuning -> error definitions
sections.output: Six forecast conditions evaluated on fourteen weeks

framework.additional_methods: KNN and random forest are standard families not fully represented by the current taxonomy leaves.
framework.composition: serial preprocessing with parallel comparator branches; XGB internally boosting
inputs: Hourly national demand, excluding export demand
modules: Construct 168/336/504/672-hour load lags and moving averages
Randomized search followed by finer grid
framework.training_inference: Hyperparameter selection uses earliest training/test pair description; older observations train models and subsequent weeks test them. Deployment origin availability of all regressors is not established by the paper.
framework.constraints: No embedded power-flow, dispatch feasibility or cost optimization constraints

dataset.name: Integrated Panama national load, pre-dispatch forecast, calendar and MERRA-2 weather
dataset.target_unit: MWh in Table 1; hourly interval energy interpreted as load by authors
dataset.split: 284 complete weeks after trimming; 14 selected test weeks, 12 monthly pre-pandemic weeks plus 2 quarantine weeks; training precedes test. Rolling CV described with 149-week window and 64 validation weeks.
dataset.preprocessing: No missing values reported; blackout outliers retained; initial 15 columns, 35 derived candidate regressors, final 13 regressors. MinMax scaling inside validation pipeline.
dataset.externality: Temporal testing in one national system, not independent country/site external validation
risks: Feature selection chronology relative to split is unclear
Weather variables are indexed at prediction time; archived real forecast availability is not established

For a single 168-hour forecast issued before a 72-hour unavailable gap, the final 72 hours of the h-168 lag would be unavailable; no explicit gap imputation/update protocol identified. Verify timeline and code before alleging leakage.
Only selected test weeks, not all future weeks

equations.label: Table 3 / MAPE
equations.audit: Definition visually includes mean and absolute relative error; Table 4 and Table 5 aggregation needs reconciliation

equations.label: Table 3 / RMSE
assumptions: Distinguish root of mean from mean of per-item roots
equations.audit: Definition is standard; Table 4 hourly-labelled distribution differs from Table 5 weekly RMSE. Actual implementation/aggregation not verified; per-item absolute error is a possible explanation, not a confirmed fact.

equations.label: Table 3 / Peak error
equations.audit: Relative absolute peak discrepancy; not time-of-peak accuracy

equations.label: Table 3 / Energy error
equations.audit: Absolute relative total-energy error can cancel signed hourly errors before absolute value

equations.label: Inline load-temperature fitted line
equations.audit: No adjustment design establishes the causal effect of temperature

experiments.rq: Which compared model forecasts weekly demand best under the stated temporal protocol?
controls: Same test weeks for model comparison
experiments.tuning: Randomized then grid search; ranges and selected parameters in Table 2; equal trial counts not reported
experiments.seed_scope: RF/XGB configuration only; not repeated stochastic experiments
experiments.runtime: Qualitative ranking only, no measured seconds
experiments.finding: Table 5: XGB average MAPE 3.74% and RMSE 55.6 versus pre-dispatch 4.95% and 71.9; does not lead all secondary metrics
experiments.boundary: No prospective untouched-test declaration or inferential significance test

experiments.rq: Where do the same forecasts fail under holiday/quarantine conditions?
experiments.finding: Selected irregular periods illustrate forecast behavior
experiments.boundary: Not a separately sampled external robustness trial; figure/text date and panel references need reconciliation

experiments.rq: Which features receive high importance within each model?
experiments.finding: Load lags important across models; calendar and weather contributions vary by model
experiments.boundary: Coefficient magnitude, tree importance and permutation importance differ in meaning. No controlled retraining ablation, no causal contribution estimate.

statistics.analysis_unit: Hourly errors for aggregate distributions; week-level metrics across 14 selected origins for Table 5
statistics.distribution: Boxplots and SD/quartiles of forecast errors; no fitted error-distribution model
statistics.estimand: Descriptive average across selected weeks; Table 4 hourly summary and Table 5 weekly summary must be distinguished
statistics.theory: Time-ordered validation; standard regression/kernel/ensemble learning; no formal statistical inference theory developed
statistics.appropriateness: Chronological validation is relevant, but hourly observations cannot be assumed independent replicates. Descriptive superiority does not imply statistically established general superiority.
statistics.effect_size_author_reported: Metric values and comparisons, no standardized inferential effect size
statistics.robustness: Selected atypical weeks and visual diagnostics only; no systematic sensitivity design
statistics.leakage_control: Scaling inside folds is described. Feature selection timing and future weather availability remain unresolved.
